inputs.message: How are roaming charges billed in Zone B?

facts: voice calls and SMS are charged at 1.5 times the standard rate
data is billed in 10MB blocks rather than continuously
outputs.reference: Zone B (Eastern Europe, parts of Asia-Pacific and Latin America) applies a 1.5x multiplier to standard voice and SMS rates, and bills data per 10MB block.

inputs.message: What are the early termination fees if a customer cancels their contract early?

facts: the fee goes down each month and reaches zero at the end of the 24-month term
the fee is based on the device subsidy still remaining, not a flat penalty
the fee is waived automatically once the customer has 24 months of tenure
outputs.reference: On a 24-month contract the fee decreases each month and reaches zero at the end of the term. It is calculated from the remaining device subsidy, so it varies by device. It is waived automatically at 24 months' tenure; before that a waiver needs supervisor approval and isn't guaranteed.

inputs.message: Which plans let unused data roll over, and for how long?

facts: only postpaid plans of 10GB or more roll unused data over
rolled-over data lasts for the next billing cycle only and is then forfeited
prepaid plans and plans under 10GB don't roll data over
outputs.reference: Postpaid plans of 10GB or more roll unused data into the next cycle only; anything not used then is forfeited. Prepaid plans and plans under 10GB have no rollover.

inputs.message: How do warranty claims work for a phone with a manufacturing defect?

facts: a manufacturing defect is repaired at no cost if the phone has no physical damage, liquid exposure or unauthorised repairs
the consultant must confirm the phone is still within its warranty or protection plan before referring it for repair
a phone that fails repeatedly with the same defect should be escalated for a replacement
outputs.reference: A manufacturing defect is repaired free under the manufacturer's warranty (typically 12 months), unless physical damage, liquid exposure or unauthorised repairs void it. Confirm the phone is still covered before referring it. Repeated failures with the same defect are escalated for a replacement.

inputs.message: When is the SIM replacement fee waived?

facts: the first replacement in any rolling 12-month window is free
a second replacement within that window costs the standard fee unless a supervisor approves a waiver
the 12-month window runs from the most recent replacement, not the calendar year
outputs.reference: The first SIM replacement in any rolling 12-month window is free. A second one in the same window costs the standard fee unless a supervisor approves a waiver. The window runs from the last replacement, not the calendar year.

inputs.message: Can I refund a $60 billing dispute myself, and how long does the customer have to file it?

facts: a dispute of $50 or more needs supervisor approval before the refund is issued
a billing dispute must be filed within 90 days of the statement date
outputs.reference: No: disputes of $50 or more need supervisor approval before refunding. The customer must file within 90 days of the statement date the charge appeared on (30 days for roaming charges).

inputs.message: Does a partial payment lift an account suspension?

facts: no, the full outstanding balance must be paid before the account is reactivated
reactivation happens once the payment has cleared, not when it is submitted
a bank transfer can take one to three business days to clear
outputs.reference: No. A suspended account is reactivated only once the full outstanding balance is paid and the payment has cleared; a bank transfer can take one to three business days to clear.

inputs.message: If a customer updates their card after a payment failed, is the failed charge retried automatically?

facts: no, a new payment attempt with the new method has to be triggered explicitly
a new payment method applies from the next scheduled charge
outputs.reference: No. Updating the payment method doesn't retry the failed charge; a new attempt must be triggered explicitly. The new method applies from the next scheduled charge.

inputs.message: What has to happen once I escalate a suspected fraud case?

facts: the escalation must be logged with a case ID within one hour
no billing changes, plan changes or password resets may be made while the case is open
normal servicing resumes only after the fraud team gives written clearance
outputs.reference: Log it with a case ID within one hour. While the case is open, make no billing changes, plan changes or password resets, even for a verified caller. Resume normal servicing only after the fraud team gives written clearance.

inputs.message: How much service credit does a customer get for an outage?

facts: the credit is proportional to how long the outage lasted
the credit is capped at one full billing cycle's charges
the outage must be confirmed by network operations as affecting the customer's area
outputs.reference: A credit proportional to the outage's duration, capped at one full billing cycle's charges. Network operations must confirm the outage in the customer's area; affected accounts are usually credited automatically in the next billing cycle.

inputs.message: Can I send a password reset by email if the customer has lost their phone?

facts: password resets are only sent by SMS to the phone number on file, not by email
if that phone can't be reached, the caller must go through the in-person or extended verification path
outputs.reference: No. After identity verification, a reset is only sent by SMS to the number on file. If that phone is lost, route the caller to the in-person or extended verification path instead.

inputs.message: If a caller fails identity verification, can I confirm whether they have an account with us?

facts: no account information may be shared, not even whether an account exists
the consultant should offer the standard alternative verification path
a suspected social-engineering attempt should be logged and escalated through the fraud process
outputs.reference: No. Share nothing, not even whether an account exists; say verification couldn't be completed and offer the standard alternative verification path. Log and escalate a suspected social-engineering attempt through the fraud process.
